AL.name: Anniston City
AL.quote: the Board permits reasonable corporal punishment of students in Anniston City schools. If such punishment is required, it shall be administered with care, tact, and caution by the principal, assistant principal, or, when appropriate, by their designee. In all cases, however, corporal punishment shall be administered in the presence of the principal or assistant principal. Corporal punishment shall not include more than three (3) licks administered to the buttocks. Other forms of corporal punishment are not permitted. In all cases, corporal punishment shall be administered only by certified personnel.
AL.notes: Anniston City Schools' site (annistonschools.com, SchoolBlocks CMS) does not surface a document library in raw HTML; the Policy Manual page embeds a Google Drive PDF viewer (drive.google.com/file/d/16fxYcM_H5l4pUoTP_Qm8DSa9LWeixJeE/preview), found via the page's embedded JSON, not a rendered link. AL.name: Butler County Schools
AL.quote: The Board shall allow reasonable corporal punishment only after other means of discipline have failed to produce desirable results. If corporal punishment is required, it shall be administered only by a certified employee in the presence of a school administrator who has been informed beforehand of the reasons for the punishment. At no time shall corporal punishment be administered in the presence of another student. Parents who object to corporal punishment as a method of discipline shall advise the school administrator in writing of the objection; however, the school administrator has the authority to determine appropriate discipline
AL.policy_code: 2026-2027 Code of Conduct, section "Corporal Punishment" (p. 14, under Formal Disciplinary Actions and Procedures)
AL.notes: Opt-out only, and non-binding: parents who object must advise the administrator in writing, but the text says the administrator retains authority to determine discipline, and the signature page reads "I DO___ or DO NOT ___ prefer that corporal punishment (paddling) be used ... However, I acknowledge the right of the school system's authority to use any and all disciplinary measures ... including paddling." Administered by a certified employee with a Board-issued paddle, no more than three licks, in the presence of a school administrator (or principal's designee), after an attempted phone call to the parent, recorded in PowerSchool, with a written explanation and witness name given to parents afterward. No disability exemption is stated. Document is the district's "2026-2027 Code of Conduct" PDF linked from https://www.butlerco.k12.al.us/for-parents/bcss-handbook-policies (BCSS Handbook & Policies page), which also lists "Board Policy/Student Handbook & Code of Conduct Revisions" dated July 17, 2025 and October 16, 2025. The Code of Conduct cites Alabama Code 16-28A-1 and Ingraham v. Wright. Corporal punishment is listed as a first-offense option for Class II (grades 6-12) and Class III offenses. No separate board policy manual (AASB-style) was found on the district site; the Code of Conduct is board-adopted and is the operative text.

AL.name: DeKalb County Board of Education (DeKalb County Schools)
AL.quote: 6.14.1 Corporal Punishment - Corporal punishment shall always be administered with a consideration for the age and physical maturity of the student. Corporal punishment must always be a deliberate, well thought out action on the part of school administrators and should be administered appropriately to effectively alter student behaviors that are unacceptable in a school environment. Should corporal punishment be needed, it must be administered according to the following: a. A student must be notified of the offense for which he/she is to receive corporal punishment and the student must be given an opportunity to explain his/her actions. b. The punishment must be administered by a school administrator and witnessed by a certified school employee. c. The punishment must be administered out of view of any other students. d. The punishment shall consist of a moderate use of physical force or physical contact by an administrator as may be necessary to maintain discipline or to enforce school rules. e. A written record of the punishment shall be made, in which the violated offense resulting in the punishment is listed along with the administered punishment, the name of the witness(es), and the name of the administrator giving the discipline. The administrator shall maintain a copy of the record and a copy shall be given to the student's parent/guardian.
AL.notes: No parental consent or opt-out; the 2026-2027 Student Handbook and Code of Conduct sec. 5.3.3 states verbatim: 'State law does not forbid corporal punishment. The DeKalb County Board of Education does not recognize a "no paddle" list. Schools must follow IEP/504 plan or make provisions for medical reasons.' Administered by a school administrator, witnessed by a certified employee, out of view of other students, written record with copy to parent. Policy manual is 'Policies and Procedures Handbook', 228 pages, cover reads 'Effective 8/1/2026' (page footers carry 'DRAFT 5/21/15' watermark). Linked from https://www.dekalbk12.org/handbooks. Companion source: 2026-2027 Student Handbook and Code of Conduct, https://files.smartsites.parentsquare.com/12948/26-27_student_handbook_final_1.pdf, sec. 5.3.3 (p. 2295 of text extraction) and the Type I / Type II offense sanction lists ('Corporal Punishment - (Witness and Due Process Required) - DeKalb County Board of Education Policy must be followed').

AL.name: Elmore County Schools
AL.quote: PROCEDURE FOR K-12 CORPORAL PUNISHMENT To maintain discipline or to enforce school rules, an administrator/designee may administer corporal punishment through reasonable use of physical force or physical contact. Corporal punishment may only replace in school suspension or a lesser consequence. It is not a substitution for placement at the Elmore County Alternative Program (ECAP). Such punishment shall be administered under conditions which do not hold up the student to ridicule or shame and punishment should never be in the presence of other students. Before corporal punishment is administered, written permission from the parent must be on file each school year.

AL.name: Houston County Schools
AL.quote: CORPORAL PUNISHMENT The Houston County Board of Education has no rule against reasonable and proper spanking/paddling of students for disciplinary reasons. Before corporal punishment is administered as a disciplinary method, the student will be given the reason for the punishment and an opportunity to explain his/her action. Corporal punishment must be administered by the administrator or by the teacher in the presence of a certified professional employee. The administrator and/or teacher will prepare a written report for each incident to be sent home on the day the corporal punishment is administered. A parent/guardian must notify the school in writing annually if he/she prohibits the school from paddling his/her student(s). The handwritten note must be delivered, in person, by the parent-by first day of each school year.
AL.notes: hcboe.us is JavaScript-rendered; resolve_handbook found nothing, so I opened the site in a browser. The homepage links 'Handbook & Code of Conduct' to this Google Doc (the doc's own header carries www.hcboe.us and its index lists 'Corporal Punishment 46'); I read it server-side via its plain-text export. This is an OPT-OUT scheme, not opt-in: corporal punishment is the default and the parent must deliver a handwritten note in person by the first day of school to prevent it, renewed annually - so 'allows', not 'consent_required'. Corporal punishment is also listed among the sanctions for Class I offenses ('Subsequent Offenses ... Corporal Punishment') and Class II offenses ('First - Student conference and parental contact, disciplinary action such as corporal punishment, ASD, ISS, bus suspension, etc.'). Everywhere I looked: (1) Forsyth's board policy manual on Simbli site 4069 — S number taken from the district's own homepage link and confirmed by resolve_handbook on https://www.forsyth.k12.ga.us; the manual header reads "Policy Listing | Forsyth County Schools". Read the complete J. Students section in a browser (34 entries, JAA through JRA): there is no JDA and no policy titled Corporal Punishment. (2) Opened Board Policy JD Student Discipline (adopted 12/31/1995, last reviewed 12/31/1995) — no corporal-punishment language, only O.C.G.A. cross-references. (3) Opened Board Policy JCD Student Conduct (adopted 12/31/1995, revised 07/31/2002) — no corporal-punishment language; the O.C.G.A. 20-2-730/731/732 citations appear only in the non-binding "Policy Reference Disclaimer" table, which the page itself says is "not intended to be part of the policy itself". (4) Opened Board Policy JCDA Student Code of Conduct (adopted 06/30/2000, revised 07/16/2015) — no corporal-punishment language. (5) Scripted a pass over all thirteen lettered sections (A-M) of the manual looking for any policy title matching corporal/paddl/spank — no hit. (6) Fetched the district's current 2026-27 Student Code of Conduct PDF, https://resources.finalsite.net/images/v1784223054/forsythk12gaus/gxs5km2nsgo4cabqy4ft/26-27CodeofConduct.pdf (resolved from https://www.forsyth.k12.ga.us/fs/resource-manager/view/d7b28113-3b63-4c12-bf88-f60711910e18): 681078 bytes, application/pdf, 24 pages, 75405 characters of text, sha256 ede367a4a5f80634de3103be13b68dd7ebb963b6615358356682c6e9a4b123ee — ZERO occurrences of "corporal", "paddl" or "spank". (7) An older BoardDocs file (go.boarddocs.com/ga/fcss/.../FY21 Coc JD and Operating Guidelines Updated.pdf) now returns HTTP 404. (8) Web search surfaced only Forsyth County, NC / Winston-Salem items. A reviewer wanting to close this should ask the district directly.

I read Section J (Students) in full in a browser -- 47 entries, JAA through JRA -- and there is NO policy titled Corporal Punishment and no JDA. Section G (Personnel) has only four entries (GAAA, GAAA-E(1), GAD, GAE) and none mention it. Board Policy JD 'Student Discipline' (ADOPTED, originally adopted 10/01/1990, last revised and reviewed 04/14/2025) was read in full: the string 'corporal' does not appear anywhere on the page. The district's SY2026-27 Code of Conduct (https://resources.finalsite.net/images/v1783626540/henryk12gaus/mpsec6pj8coggpjt24jm/SY2026-27CodeofConduct_weblinks_FINAL.pdf, reached via https://www.henry.k12.ga.us/fs/resource-manager/view/789ef6d8-0848-4275-9406-9ddfcf9950b8; fetch_document: 782,449 bytes, application/pdf, 35 pages, 146,475 chars) returned ZERO hits for 'corporal punishment', 'paddl' and 'spank'. Simbli's built-in full-text search would settle whether the phrase appears in some other section, but the search panel would not submit under automation, and fetch_simbli_policy was bot-challenged throughout this session. Filed unknown rather than 'bans' as the legacy map claimed, because nothing I opened says so.

GA.notes: Opt-out district, so 'allows'. Source is the JDHS Student Handbook (26-27), the PDF behind http://hs.jeff-davis.k12.ga.us/apps/pages/index.jsp?uREC_ID=2031192&type=d&pREC_ID=2108368 (Edlio file host, listed by the brief as machine-fetchable). fetch_document: application/pdf, 1,379,549 bytes, 53 pages, text layer present. The quoted sentence is on page 41, in the Student Code of Conduct definitions, immediately after 'Corporal Punishment - Moderate use of physical force or physical contact by a principal or designee in the presence of another school official as may be necessary to maintain discipline or to enforce school rules.' Corporal punishment is listed as an available disciplinary action for any violation of the Code of Conduct (page 35), as the disciplinary action for Level I offenses (page 36) and as the first and subsequent offense penalty for Level II offenses (page 38). The handbook is district-wide in substance: it carries the Jeff Davis County School System mission, nondiscrimination notice, admission rules and the board's code of conduct, and cites board policy by code elsewhere (e.g. 'Jeff Davis Co. Bd. of Ed. Policy JCDA 12-08-08' for verbal assault); no policy code is printed against the corporal punishment entry, and no adoption or revision date appears on the document (the web page it hangs off was published 2026-07-24). CAVEAT for the reviewer: the board's own policy manual is on Simbli at https://simbli.eboardsolutions.com/Policy/PolicyListing.aspx?S=4093 (site number confirmed both from the district's own 'Policies' link and independently by resolve_handbook). fetch_simbli_policy for site 4093 returned Imperva's bot-challenge page on every attempt over several hours of spaced retries, so the board policy itself (Georgia code JD/JDA) has not been read and its adoption date is unknown. The next contributor should open that Simbli listing once the vendor's rate limit clears.

GA.name: Laurens County Schools
GA.quote: Any principal or other designated school administrator employed by the Board of Education, in order to maintain proper control and discipline over pupils under his or her care and supervision, may, in the exercise of sound discretion, administer corporal punishment to any pupil or pupils under his or her care and supervision.
GA.notes: Opt-out: "Corporal punishment shall not be administered to a child whose parents or legal guardian have filed with the principal of the school a statement expressly objecting to the use of corporal punishment or a statement from a medical doctor licensed in Georgia stating that corporal punishment is detrimental to the child's mental or emotional stability." Only a principal or designated administrator may administer it, never a teacher or parent; it must be witnessed by another certified employee informed beforehand in the pupil's presence; a written explanation and the witness's name are provided to parents on request; it may not be excessive and generally not a first-line punishment. No IEP/504 exemption beyond the doctor's-statement route. Simbli/eBoard (GSBA) board policy manual, site S=4101, reached from https://www.lcboe.net/338421_2 (Board of Education page, link 'eBoard - Laurens County' -> https://simbli.eboardsolutions.com/Index.aspx?S=4101). Policy JDA status ADOPTED, Original Adopted Date 02/14/2008, Last Reviewed Date 08/13/2020. References O.C.G.A. 20-2-730 through 20-2-732. Simbli listing is JavaScript-rendered; the ViewPolicy link was obtained by filtering the listing to section J in a browser.

GA.name: Tift County Schools
GA.quote: Corporal punishment may be administered by the building principal or designee to a pupil for an infraction of school rules.  Corporal punishment will always be administered in the presence of a witness who must be a member of the school faculty. Corporal punishment, when administered to a female student, must be administered by a female faculty member.  In all cases involving corporal punishment, a written report will be kept on file in the principal's office.
GA.notes: AGENT-ATTESTED, NEEDS HUMAN CONFIRMATION: the source is JavaScript-only and refused every automated read, so the policy was transcribed from a browser. Board Policy JDA 'Corporal Punishment', status ADOPTED, Original Adopted Date 07/12/1977, Last Revised Date 04/16/2020, Last Reviewed Date 04/16/2020. Classified 'allows' (OPT-OUT, not opt-in): the policy authorises corporal punishment by default and withholds it only where parents have said otherwise -- verbatim, 'Corporal punishment shall not be administered to a child whose parents, or legal guardian, have stated they do not desire paddling used as punishment for their child.' The policy also states, verbatim, 'Corporal punishment shall never be used as a first line of punishment for misbehavior with two (2) exceptions;' and '*The Superintendent will ensure there are clear procedures in the board approved student handbook for implementation of this policy.' S number 4157 is Tift County Schools' Simbli site and the page header reads 'Tift County Schools'. NOT machine-fetchable: Simbli is JavaScript-only behind an Imperva challenge and fetch_simbli_policy for site 4157 returned the bot-challenge error, so I read the policy in a real browser and supply the full verbatim text in source_text.

TX.name: Paris ISD
TX.quote: Corporal punishment may be used as a discipline management technique in accordance with this policy and the Student Code of Conduct. Corporal punishment shall not be administered to a student whose parent has submitted to the principal a signed statement for the current school year prohibiting the use of corporal punishment with his or her child. The parent may reinstate permission to use corporal punishment at any time during the school year by submitting a signed statement to the principal.
TX.notes: Confirms the legacy 'allows' value with a source and quote. Opt-out, not opt-in: a parent must submit a signed statement to the principal each school year to prohibit it and may reinstate permission at any time. Guidelines: limited to spanking or paddling; the student is told the reason first; administered only by the principal or designee; instrument approved by the principal; administered in the presence of one other District professional employee in a designated place out of view of other students. No same-sex-administrator clause. Disciplinary record must include the administrator, the witness, and the date and time. No disability exemption in FO(LOCAL); FO(LEGAL) carries the Education Code 37.0011 parent-statement text. Read on TASB Policy Online, Paris ISD Board Policy Manual key=786 (https://pol.tasb.org/Home/Index/786). Footer: UPDATE 126, DATE ISSUED: 11/10/2025. Corporal punishment shall not be administered to a student whose parent has submitted to the principal a signed statement for the current school year prohibiting the use of corporal punishment with his or her child. The parent may reinstate permission to use corporal punishment at any time during the school year by submitting a signed statement to the principal.

contact.mailing_address: P.O. Box 869, 103 Sloan Street, Pineland, TX 75968

TX.notes: Read via crew fetch_tasb_policy tool, TASB Policy Online district key 1046 (West Sabine ISD confirmed by page header, found by bisecting pol.tasb.org/Home/Index/<key> between Balmorhea ISD key=1020/Reeves Co. and Shepherd ISD key=1050/San Jacinto Co.). FO(LOCAL) shows standard opt-out corporal punishment: allowed unless parent files a signed statement prohibiting it for that school year -> classified 'allows' per project rule (opt-out is allows). Policy manual Update 126, date issued 10/28/2025 (this is the printed revision date on the policy page, not confirmed as a distinct board adoption date). District's own site (westsabineisd.net) answers a 3,038-byte Imperva/Fastly JS challenge stub to plain curl; content confirmed instead via r.jina.ai reader proxy and the Thrillshare CMS API (thrillshare-cmsv2.services.thrillshare.com/api/v2/s/151047/documents) for contact/board info.
